evidence.note: New table-driven test suite for the kind registry: decode caps, reduce/union cliffs, match-then-adjudicate composition, still-present, prompt fencing and cmd. Verified against internal/fsm/kind/kind.go behaviour.
New tests for terminal run-row emission: golden row bytes, verdict/status mapping, torn-tail repair, idempotency, and write-error paths against internal/fsm/record/record.go.

External hash-chain oracle fixture; regenerated by testdata/oracle.sh with a non-Go sha256 and consumed by internal/fsm/run/store_test.go:799 TestOracle, which re-derives every prev and the canonical form. Genuinely external, not self-referential.

Doc claims checked against the implementation: /fsm exit-code table, the override request/grant separation (internal/findings/override.go:107 refuses a self-grant, RequestOverride persists --escalation at override.go:77), the 120,000-byte diff cap and 4,000-byte untracked cap (internal/gitcontext/gitcontext.go:15-17, internal/contextprofile/profile.go:21-23), and the shard result path (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:448,474). All accurate.

Validation evidence: `go test -cover ./internal/fsm/record/... ./internal/fsm/kind/... ./internal/fsm/run/...` passes at 100.0% of statements in all three packages; `go test -count=2 -shuffle=on` also passes, so the package-global seams these tests swap do not currently create order dependence.

findings.note: Package-level seams are swapped without restore. record_test.go:157 assigns `nanos = func() int64 { return 42 }` with no defer/t.Cleanup, so the torn-fragment clock stays pinned at 42 for every later test in the package (two torn fragments written after this point would collide on the filename `runs.jsonl-42`). record_test.go:276-281 saves and restores `flock`, but only on the success path: the t.Fatalf at line 279 would leave the failing stub installed for the remaining assertions in TestWriteErrors, turning one failure into a misleading cascade. Verified latent only: `go test -count=2 -shuffle=on ./internal/fsm/record/...` passes today.

Dead test fixture: kind_test.go:228-232 builds a 20,000-element []run.BugStatus named fatSt and then discards it with `_ = fatSt`. Nothing is asserted, so this is an abandoned status-payload-cap case that only costs allocation time. Either finish the assertion (a StillPresent payload over MaxPayload should fail Decode with reason "cap") or delete the block.

Comment names a boundary the test does not pin. kind_test.go:203 says "canonical payload cap: 63 x MaxText fits, 64 does not", but the passing assertion at line 209 uses fat[:60], not 63. I confirmed by probe that 60, 61, 62 and 63 all decode and 64 fails with ERR_NODE_OUTPUT_INVALID (reason=cap, "output exceeds 262016 bytes"), so the comment is factually right — but a regression that dropped the effective cap to 61 or 62 findings would still pass this test. Use fat[:63] for the ok case.

Comment overstates what is exercised. kind_test.go:540 reads "256 ok, 257 refused before any call", but TestK4StillPresent only builds bugs(0, 257) and asserts the 257 refusal; the accepted 256 case is never run through the still-present executor (the 256/257 union cliff is covered separately in TestK2Reduce for adjudicate and cmd, not for still-present). Either add the 256 case or drop the claim from the comment.
